chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We visit the mosques around the city, so which one should I start with? He said: 'Start with Quba and pray in it and increase [prayer], for it is the first mosque in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed in this area.
Then go to the Mashrabah of Umm Ibrahim (peace be upon her) and pray in it, for it is the dwelling place of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his place of prayer.
Then you come to the Mosque of Fadikh and pray in it, for your Prophet has prayed in it.
When you have finished this side, you come to the side of Uhud, and you start with the mosque that is below the Harra, and you pray in it.
Then you pass by the grave of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (peace be upon him) and send greetings upon him.
Then you pass by the graves of the martyrs and stand by them and say: Peace be upon you, O people of the dwellings, you are forerunners for us and we will surely follow you.
Then you come to the mosque in the spacious place next to the mountain on your right when you enter Uhud, and pray in it.
For it is there that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went out to Uhud where he met the polytheists, and they did not leave until the prayer time arrived, so he prayed in it.
Then pass by again until you return, and pray at the graves of the martyrs as much as Allah has decreed for you.
Then proceed on your way until you come to the Mosque of the Confederates (Al-Ahzab), and pray in it and supplicate to Allah in it.
For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated in it on the Day of the Confederates.

And he said: 'O Cryer of those who cry for help, and O Responder of those in distress, and O Helper of those in anxiety, remove my grief, my worry, and my distress, for you see my condition and the condition of my companions.'

key_terms.أُمِّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Umm Ibrahim (mother of the Prophet's son)
key_terms.مَشْرَبَةَ: Mashrabah (a place of prayer or dwelling)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَحْزَابِ: Day of the Confederates (Battle of Khandaq)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order for visiting mosques and graves in Medina according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a specific *ziyarat* (visitation) route for Medina, emphasizing the spiritual merit of praying at sites directly associated with the Prophet’s life and battles, such as Uhud and the trench. It highlights the Shia practice of linking physical spaces with historical religious events, culminating in a supplication at Masjid Al-Ahzab that mirrors the Prophet’s invocation during the Battle of the Confederates. This itinerary serves not only as a devotional act but also as a means of reconnecting with the foundational history of the Islamic community.
